root_cause_label: ALS Low-Rank Factorization Instead of Nuclear-Norm Matrix Completion With Hard Equality Constraints + Premature Completion Without Verifying Observed-Entry Constraint Satisfaction
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent selects ALS-based matrix factorization (which does not enforce exact equality at observed entries) instead of the benchmark-required nuclear-norm minimization with hard equality constraints, then declares completion without verifying reconstruction fidelity.
t_err_evidence: Step 5 implements ALS low-rank factorization (rank=15, L2 regularization, mean-centering) and writes solution_0.txt through solution_19.txt; this is a heuristic approach that does not enforce X[r_k, c_k] == observed_k and does not match the benchmark's nuclear-norm minimization objective.
t_commit_evidence: Step 5 writes all 20 solution files using the wrong algorithm; after this step the incorrect outputs are committed to disk and the agent treats the task as essentially done, with no plan to revise the method.
t_surface_evidence: Step 7 is the completion claim where the agent asserts the task is done without any evidence of passing the hidden evaluator; the failure is observable at the point of premature finalization.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge about the specific algorithmic requirement of the benchmark (convex nuclear-norm minimization with hard equality constraints on observed entries). It applies the well-known ALS heuristic instead, which optimizes a different objective and does not guarantee exact constraint satisfaction at observed positions.
